life_summary: Merrill Russell Ballard was born on October 8, 1928, in Salt Lake City, Utah. He grew up in a prominent LDS family with deep roots in church leadership and community service. Ballard received his education in Salt Lake City and developed a career as a prominent businessman and church administrator. He married Barbara Bowen on August 28, 1951, in the Salt Lake Temple, and the couple raised seven children together. Barbara preceded him in death on October 1, 2018, after more than six decades of marriage. Ballard established himself as a respected leader in both business and ecclesiastical circles, becoming a trusted figure in church administration and governance throughout his adult life.
church_summary: M. Russell Ballard served as a missionary in England from 1948 to 1950, serving as a counselor in the mission presidency. He was called to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles on October 6, 1985, and served in this capacity for 38 years until his death in 2023. Ballard served as President of the Canada Toronto Mission from 1974 to 1976 and held the position of Acting President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles from 2018 until his death. He also served as editor of church magazines from 1980 to 1984. As an apostle, he was sustained by church members as a prophet, seer, and revelator, and played a significant role in church administration and policy implementation.
